steps.title: Factor the numerator f(x)
steps.content:
Start by factoring $f(x) = x^3 - 9x$.

Factor out $x$ first:
$$x^3 - 9x = x(x^2 - 9)$$

Then factor the difference of squares:
$$x^2 - 9 = (x-3)(x+3)$$

So: $f(x) = x(x-3)(x+3)$

steps.title: Factor the denominator g(x)
steps.content:
Now factor $g(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3$.

Find two numbers that multiply to $-3$ and add to $-2$: those are $-3$ and $+1$.

$$x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x-3)(x+1)$$

steps.title: Form the ratio and cancel common factors
steps.content:
Write the full fraction:
$$\frac{f(x)}{g(x)} = \frac{x(x-3)(x+3)}{(x-3)(x+1)}$$

Since $x > 3$, we know $x \neq 3$, so $(x-3) \neq 0$ and we can cancel it:
$$= \frac{x(x+3)}{x+1}$$

steps.title: Match to the answer choices
steps.content:
The simplified expression is:
$$\frac{x(x+3)}{x+1}$$

This matches answer choice **D**: $\dfrac{x \times (x+3)}{x+1}$.

c04ab16e-bdaf-4d80-bc91-c76920ba76d1.key_insight: The key is recognizing that $(x-3)$ is a factor in both the numerator and denominator, allowing cancellation only because $x > 3$ guarantees the factor is nonzero.

why_wrong.label: A
why_wrong.reason: This would result from incorrectly canceling all factors of $x$, $(x-3)$, and $(x+3)$ except $\frac{1}{x+1}$, which loses the $x(x+3)$ in the numerator.

why_wrong.label: B
why_wrong.reason: This drops the factor of $x$ from the numerator entirely, keeping only $\frac{x+3}{x+1}$ instead of $\frac{x(x+3)}{x+1}$.

why_wrong.label: C
why_wrong.reason: This expression incorrectly splits the fraction and adds 1 separately, which is not equivalent to the original ratio. The algebra used to arrive at this form is invalid.
